source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 365 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Article heading
sections.text:
ARTICLE 365.

PD 365.

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 365 was established by Ordinance No. 21182, passed by the Dallas City Council on January 22, 1992. Ordinance No. 21182 amended Ordinance No. 19455, Chapter 51A of the Dallas City Code, as amended. Ordinance No. 21182 was amended by Ordinance No. 22542, passed by the Dallas City Council on September 13, 1995, and Ordinance No. 23403, passed by the Dallas City Council on January 14, 1998. (Ord. Nos. 19455; 21182; 22542; 23403; 25850)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 365 is established on property generally located along the west line of Campbell Road, north of the north line of Preston Fairways Drive. The size of PD 365 is approximately 5.571 acres. (Ord. Nos. 21182; 25850)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions contained in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to code articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) Section 51A-2.101, “Interpretations,” applies to this article.

(d) For purposes of determining the applicability of regulations in this article and in Chapter 51A triggered by adjacency or proximity to another zoning district, and for purposes of interpreting the DIR and RAR requirements of Division 51A-4.800, this district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. Nos. 21182; 25850)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.104. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

Use and development of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit 365A). (Ord. Nos. 21182; 23403; 25850)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.105. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Private streets or alleys are permitted by right.

(b) All other uses permitted in the TH-3(A) Townhouse District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the TH-3(A) Townhouse District, as set out in the Dallas Development Code. For example, a use only permitted in the TH-3(A) Townhouse District by specific use permit (SUP) is only permitted in this PD by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the TH-3(A) Townhouse District is subject to DIR in this PD; etc. (Ord. Nos. 22542; 25850)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.106. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations contained in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217. (Ord. Nos. 21182; 25850)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.107. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations contained in Division 51A-4.400. In the event of a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 10 feet from a public or private street or access easement.

(b) Side and rear yards. Minimum rear yard is five feet. Minimum side yard adjacent to an alley is five feet. Minimum side yard adjacent to public right-of-way is 10 feet. For Lots 48 through 57, no minimum interior side yard setback from the lot lines designated on the development plan, provided a five foot side yard setback is provided on the opposite interior side lot line.

(c) Setbacks.

(1) Minimum setback from the screening wall located along Campbell Road is 10 feet.

(2) Any enclosed parking space with an entry facing an access easement must be setback a minimum of 25 feet from the easement.

(d) Dwelling unit density. No maximum dwelling unit density.

(e) Number of dwelling units permitted. No more than 31 dwelling units are permitted on the Property.

(f) Floor area ratio. No maximum floor area ratio.

(g) Height. Maximum structure height is 36 feet.

(h) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 50 percent.

(i) Lot size. No minimum lot size.

(j) Stories. Maximum number of stories above grade is two. (Ord. Nos. 21182; 23403; 25850)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.108. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Two off-street parking spaces must be provided for each single family dwelling. These spaces may be tandem spaces. Off-street parking for all other uses must be provided in accordance with the Dallas Development Code.

(b) Off-street loading must be provided in accordance with the Dallas Development Code. (Ord. Nos. 21182; 25850)

sections.title: Sidewalks
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.109. SIDEWALKS.

Five-foot-wide sidewalks must be provided as shown on the development plan. Except as otherwise provided in this article, sidewalks must be constructed and maintained to the standards for sidewalks in the public right-of-way. (Ord. Nos. 21182; 25850)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. Nos. 21182; 25850)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.111. SIGNS.

All signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts contained in Article VII. (Ord. Nos. 21182; 25850)

sections.title: Frontage
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.112. FRONTAGE.

Frontage must be provided as required by the development plan. In the event of a conflict between this condition and Section 51A-8.503, this condition controls. (Ord. Nos. 21182; 25850)

sections.title: Access Easements
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.113. ACCESS EASEMENTS.

(a) Each lot must be served by an access easement that runs with the land and is indicated on the plat. All access easements must be a minimum of 24 feet in width, and must have access to a dedicated public or private street.

(b) A mutual access agreement creating a 24-foot-wide common access way to Campbell Road from the Property must be executed and filed in accordance with this section prior to approval of the final plat. The agreement must be:

(1) in writing and be signed by all owners of the properties affected;

(2) a covenant running with the land;

(3) approved by both the building official and the city attorney; and

(4) filed in the deed records of the county in which the properties affected are located. The agreement shall not be considered effective until it is filed in the deed records in accordance with this section. After the mutual access agreement is filed in the deed records, two file-marked copies of the agreement must be filed with the building official.

(c) Except as otherwise provided in this section, the common access way must be constructed and maintained to the standards for public rights-of-way and must be approved by the director of public works and transportation. Sidewalks are required and must be constructed and maintained in

accordance with Section 51P-365.109. Water and sanitary sewer mains must be installed in accordance with the applicable ordinances.

(d) A legal entity must be created that is responsible for the maintenance of the common access way and its adjacent sidewalks, and the installation and maintenance of interior traffic control devices. The legal instruments establishing the responsibility for the common access way must be submitted to the city plan commission for approval, be approved as to legal form by the city attorney, and recorded in the appropriate county.

(e) Access easements must contain private service easements including, but not limited to, the following:

(1) All franchised corporations or companies, including utility and communication companies.

(2) Fire lane.

(3) Street lighting.

(4) Government vehicle access.

(5) Mail collection and delivery access.

(6) Utility meter reading access.

(f) Streets lights comparable with those required on public rights-of-way must be provided. Street lighting design plans must be approved by the director of public works and transportation.

(g) Design plans and location of all traffic control devices must be approved by the traffic engineer. The design, size, color, and construction of all traffic control devices must comply with those required in public rights-of-way.

(h) The fire protection standards in Article XIII of the Dallas Fire Code must be followed.

(i) Access easements and the area they serve must be platted.

(j) Guard houses may be constructed at any entrance to the common access way. All guard houses must be at least 25 feet from a public right-of-way.

(k) Any structure that restricts access to the common access way must provide a passageway 20 feet wide and 14 feet high.

(l) One entrance to the common access way must remain open at all times. If an additional entrance is closed at any time, it must be constructed to permit opening of the passageway in emergencies by boltcutters or breakaway panels.

(m) The city has no obligation to maintain the common access way. If the common access way is not maintained in compliance with the requirements of this section, the city, after a public hearing before the city plan commission, shall have the right, but not the obligation, to take those actions necessary to put the common access way in compliance. The legal entity responsible for maintaining the common access way shall pay the city for the work performed within a period of 180 days from the presentation of the bill. (Ord. Nos. 21182; 25850)

sections.title: Ingress And Egress
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.114. INGRESS AND EGRESS.

Ingress and egress between the Property and Campbell Road must be provided as shown on Exhibit 365B. (Ord. Nos. 22542; 25850)

sections.title: Visual Obstruction Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.115. VISUAL OBSTRUCTION REGULATIONS.

With the exception of the improvements identified on Exhibit 365B, all improvements must comply with the visual obstruction regulations contained in Section 51A-4.602(d). (Ord. Nos. 22542; 25850)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.116. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Existing landscaping along the existing walls, as indicated on the Exhibit 365B, must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition.

(b) Landscaping installed in the island, as shown on Exhibit 365B, must not exceed 30 inches in height. (Ord. Nos. 22542; 25850)

sections.title: Private Streets And Alleys
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.117. PRIVATE STREETS AND ALLEYS.

Private streets must comply with the provisions of Section 51A-8.604(d). (Ord. Nos. 22542; 25850)

sections.title: General Requirements
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.118. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the requirements of all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all applicable ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 22542; 25850)

sections.title: Paving
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.119. PAVING.

All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation. (Ord. Nos. 22542; 25850)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.120. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

The building official shall not issue a building permit or certificate of occupancy for a use in this PD until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other applicable ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 22542; 25850)

sections.title: Zoning Map
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-365.121. ZONING MAP.

PD 365 is located on Zoning Map No. A-7. (Ord. Nos. 21182; 25850)
